about: Five generations of the Wagner family have grown grapes on the eastern slope of Seneca Lake. Bill Wagner, a lifelong Lodi resident and grower, broke ground on a winery even before New York’s Farm Winery Act of 1976 passed, building it largely with his own family; the first vintage was 1978 and the doors opened in June 1979, when the Finger Lakes had barely a dozen wineries. He designed the distinctive eight-sided winery building himself, and today the estate farms about 250 acres.

Vidal Blanc is a hardy French hybrid prized in cold climates for its thick skin and high natural acidity, which keeps sweet wines fresh. For this ice wine the fruit is frozen and then gently pressed, so much of the water stays behind as ice crystals and only concentrated juice runs from the press. In 2021 the sugar rose from 19.4° Brix at harvest to 37° at pressing. The wine is fermented and kept in stainless steel and finishes at about 12.8% alcohol with roughly 16.5% residual sugar.

Wagner describes light floral aromas with fresh, lingering flavours of ripe pear and citrus, and suggests serving it alongside a favourite dessert or on its own as dessert. Vidal’s acidity is what keeps all that sweetness from feeling heavy. Like most ice wines it is bottled in half bottles and made in small lots; Wagner’s recent vintages have run to around a thousand cases.
facts: Pressed from frozen grapes; 19.4° Brix at harvest to 37° at pressing
